reading.body:
Deb Fischer's recorded AI record is one bill and two $2,500 checks, not a broad pattern of AI legislation.

The fourteen events are almost entirely a single bill, S. 2296, tracked across ten procedural and amendment votes on 2025-10-09, plus three earlier votes on the same bill in September 2025. She voted Yea on the motion to proceed, on cloture, on tabling an amendment, and on final passage, and split her votes across the October amendments. That is a voting record on one measure, not a portfolio of AI bills.

The money is two contributions of $2,500 each, from the Meta Platforms PAC in December 2025 and the Amazon PAC in February 2025. Both are corporate PAC donations at identical amounts, and the data records no other AI-company or AI-focused committee money. Nothing here establishes what S. 2296 does, whether it concerns AI at all, or whether either contribution relates to any vote. The dates are placed in order for reading, and the data itself makes no causal claim.

For AI specifically, this shows the legislative and funding footprint around one senator is thin and concentrated. It does not show committee assignments, sponsored AI bills, or any position on data centers, power, or compute. A reader should treat this as a dated index of records, not as evidence about influence or intent.
